guide.summary: Private app, own workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public unlisted app for customers (app review, wait up to 7 business days per review round); Public app listed in the App Store (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.

composio.note: Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. For launch, use your own app so users see your brand and you get dedicated quota.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio manages an Intercom OAuth app. For production, bring your own app: managed apps share quota and show a Composio consent message.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio, not your brand, with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers
You control the scopes that Intercom reviews

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace and developer account
prerequisites.detail: Private apps use a paid workspace, and any use of the Intercom Service requires Intercom's subscription terms.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URLs
prerequisites.detail: Intercom requires HTTPS redirect URLs. You can list testing and production URLs.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account, provide test credentials or setup instructions in the app description.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: In the Developer Hub, create the app and tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page.
steps.done_when: OAuth sections for redirect URLs and permissions appear

steps.title: Pick minimal scopes
steps.detail: Draft the smallest scope list that covers the agent's tools, with a written justification for each.
steps.done_when: Scope list and justifications are ready

steps.title: Add redirect URL from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it under Redirect URLs, then select scopes by checkbox.
steps.done_when: Redirect URL and scopes are saved

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret from the Basic Information page.

steps.title: Prepare review video script
steps.detail: Write a script showing OAuth install, full app functionality and OAuth uninstall, with the full client_id and state visible in the OAuth URL.

steps.title: Record the video
steps.detail: Record the demo. An incomplete video must be resubmitted.

steps.title: Fill forms and submit for review
steps.detail: Complete the App Partner Program form with company details and use cases, then click Submit for Review.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. If rejected, fix issues and resubmit.

steps.title: Complete App Store listing
steps.detail: Fill out listing pages and Installation status, then select List in App store.

steps.title: Generate private access token
steps.detail: Generate the token in the Intercom dashboard for your own workspace.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejections
traps.detail: They are the most common reason for initial rejection. Intercom may also approve fewer permissions than requested, limiting your credentials.

traps.title: Incomplete video forces resubmission
traps.detail: Show all functionality and OAuth install and uninstall, or you must resubmit.

traps.title: Intercom name in app name is banned
traps.detail: Do not use the Intercom name or logo in your app name or logo.

traps.title: Wrong regional host for Google sign-in
traps.detail: EU and AU customers are normally prompted for region, but Google sign-in fails if the host does not match.

traps.title: Broken install links reject listings
traps.detail: Broken or unclear installation links cause rejection and resubmission.

traps.title: Approval is revocable
traps.detail: Intercom can revoke credentials after approval if the app or your security policies are non-compliant.

traps.title: Do not share one token across users
traps.detail: You need an access token for each end user and may not let others use it.

blockers.what_it_means: Intercom found issues such as excess scopes, an incomplete video or broken links.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit. Allow up to seven business days again.
blockers.agent_can_help: Trim scopes and rewrite justifications; check the video script against requirements.

blockers.symptom: Customers cannot install the app yet
blockers.what_it_means: While under review the app is private to you and your team.
blockers.what_to_do: Wait for approval; test in a staging app meanwhile.

open_questions: How long does the App Store listing decision take? Not documented; ask Intercom developer support.
Do real review times match the seven business day figure? No independent timing was found; ask other developers or Intercom support.
Does Intercom require a paid workspace to build or test a public OAuth app? Docs only state this for private apps; check in the Developer Hub.
